CalculateDensity:
Calculate static periodic-cell mass density with complete source provenance.

Args:
    file_name: Existing periodic structure file supported by pymatgen,
        such as CIF or POSCAR; absolute path or task attachment name.

    numbers; sites, formula, source_file, source_sha256 and method. Density
    uses occupancy-weighted cell mass and the supplied cell volume. It is
    not a measured bulk/powder density, porosity estimate or relaxed state.

Raises:
    FileNotFoundError: Missing source file.
    ValueError: Unreadable structure, nonpositive/nonfinite volume or mass,
        or a source file that changes while it is being read. No error is
        returned as a successful density observation.

CompareMolecularShapes: Compare 2-100 conformers by typed USRCAT/GetUSRScore, with declared geometry policy. source_format=smiles takes a list; sdf takes an uploaded SDF path. generate builds ETKDGv3 conformers with seed/optimization/H policy for both input forms. preserve is SDF-only, requires as_parsed H and no optimization, and uses the supplied coordinates unchanged. Every invalid record is an error; no silent filtering/re-embedding. Returns a symmetric USRCAT similarity matrix and explicit index mapping. Fingerprint/Tanimoto comparisons are a separate API.

ElementwiseNumericOperations: Apply one explicitly selected arithmetic transformation to a finite vector or matrix, preserving shape and order. Validate operand shape, mathematical domain and finite representability; do not generate code.
ElementwiseNumericOperations(operation: str, values: list, other: list | float | None=None) -> dict
operation: str; values: list; other: list | float | None

Apply one declared arithmetic operation to a numeric vector or matrix.

Args:
    operation: add/subtract/multiply/divide use values as the left operand.
        sqrt/log/exp/reciprocal/abs are unary. log is the natural logarithm.
    values: A nonempty 1D vector or nonempty rectangular 2D matrix, with at
        most 10000 total finite real entries in scientific row/column order.
        Ragged, mixed vector/matrix, empty rows and deeper nesting fail.
        Booleans/null/strings are rejected. Arithmetic is ordinary float64,
        not arbitrary-precision integer or symbolic arithmetic.
    other: For binary operations, either one finite numeric scalar broadcast
        to every row, or a finite vector of EXACTLY the same length. A
        one-element list is not broadcast. For a 2D matrix, other may be
        a scalar or an exactly matching rectangular 2D matrix; 1D vectors,
        single-row/column broadcasting and all implicit axis expansion fail. Unary operations require null.

Returns:
    dict with operation, values (same ordered shape, all finite floats),
    length (outer length), shape, element_count, operand_mode
    (unary/scalar_broadcast/aligned_vector/aligned_matrix), and scope.
    No file, network, code generation, expression evaluation, model fitting
    or unit inference occurs. Callers must establish compatible quantities,
    record alignment and meaningful transformations from scientific context.

Raises:
    ValueError: Invalid length/type/operation, zero division, negative square
        root, nonpositive logarithm, overflow/nonfinite result, or a nonzero
        multiply/divide/exp result that underflows to zero. Failing element
        indices are zero-based row-major indices.
        Entire calls fail; invalid rows are not dropped, clipped or imputed.

FinitePopulationCoverage: Compute hypergeometric zero-hit probabilities and expected observed-feature coverage under uniform sampling without replacement from an explicit finite population. Feature overlaps are allowed; no unseen-feature estimate or inference is provided.
FinitePopulationCoverage(population_size: int, feature_success_counts: list, sample_sizes: list) -> dict
population_size: int; feature_success_counts: list[int]; sample_sizes: list[int]

Expected distinct features encountered in a uniform sample without replacement.

population_size is an integer number of exchangeable sampling units,0..1e9.
Each integer feature_success_counts[k] is the number of those units carrying
feature k,0..population_size. Features may overlap: the expectation uses
linearity and does not assume mutual independence or mutually exclusive
categories. Caller must establish the actual scientific sampling unit.

sample_sizes contains integer draws,each0..population_size;its order and
duplicates are retained. Both lists have1..1000entries and their product is
at most10000. At most2000000log-product terms are evaluated per call.
Mathematically integral finite JSON numbers such as448.0 are accepted and
converted without loss to integers;fractions,booleans and strings reject.

For a feature present in K of N units and draw m,the probability of no hit is
C(N-K,m)/C(N,m). Zero and certain-hit boundaries are evaluated exactly. Other
cases use a finite log1p product with min(K,m) terms and -expm1(logP) for
stable tiny hit probabilities. No simulation,normal approximation or silent
probability clipping is used. This is the hypergeometric zero-hit formula.

Returns population/feature counts and ordered analyses. Every analysis has
sample_size,sample_fraction(null if N=0),feature_absence_probabilities in the
original feature order,expected_detected_features,and
expected_fraction_of_observed_features(null if every feature count is0).
Expected values are finite real numbers,not rounded observed counts.

This computes an expectation conditional on the supplied finite population
and uniform sampling model. It provides no confidence interval,p-value,
unseen-feature estimate,detection correction,spatial independence proof,
extrapolation beyond N,or guarantee of population representativeness.

FitParametricCurve: Fit one explicitly selected fixed-family curve by bounded local least squares. Return fitted parameters and numerical diagnostics; optimization convergence is not a proof of scientific model validity.

FitParametricCurve(x: list, y: list, model_type: str, initial_parameters: list, lower_bounds: list | None=None, upper_bounds: list | None=None, sigma: list | None=None, absolute_sigma: bool=False, loss: str='linear', max_evaluations: int=2000) -> dict
x: list; y: list; model_type: str; initial_parameters: list; lower_bounds: list | None; upper_bounds: list | None; sigma: list | None; absolute_sigma: bool; loss: str; max_evaluations: int

Fit one declared fixed curve family using bounded local least squares.

Families/formula/parameter order are public REGISTRY. There are2 or3 fitted
parameters, at most1000 observations, and observations must exceed parameter
count. Duplicate x observations are allowed; at least2 distinct x are needed.
Optional sigma are positive observation standard deviations, not weights;
residuals are divided by sigma. No weights are estimated. Absolute_sigma
affects approximate covariance scaling only. Bounds may narrow but never
widen family domains; per-entry null means the family's default bound.
Linear, soft_l1 or huber loss uses fixed f_scale1 in sigma-scaled units.
Return local optimizer diagnostics even when not converged; success only
means numeric termination, never global optimum or scientific applicability.
Approximate local covariance is supplied only for converged, full-column-rank,
interior linear-loss fits with residual df>0. It assumes independent errors,

Get one final core crystal structure for a single Materials Project ID.

Queries only the official materials/core endpoint; this is its current
final material structure, not necessarily the geometry of another property
calculation or a surface slab. Legacy numeric mp-/mvc- IDs and current
eight-letter mp- IDs are accepted. Aliases are reported as requested and
resolved IDs. No fallback to another property endpoint is performed.

    material_id (str): One bare legal material ID; no list, formula or query.
Returns:

    retained), resolved/requested material IDs, source hash and provenance. Cell
    lengths/angles/volume and fractional/Cartesian coordinates are checked
    with roundoff tolerances. Site coordinates may differ by integer cell
    images only along periodic axes (pbc defaults to all true if absent).
    Missing, ambiguous, malformed, authorization or HTTP responses raise
    explicit exceptions; no None or fabricated structure is returned.

MatchedPeriodicDisplacements:
Return minimum-image displacements for fixed same-index crystal sites.

CIF fractional positions are preserved without rational-coordinate snapping.

Both explicitly uploaded ordered structures must contain the same species
sequence, 1..256 sites and a common cell (absolute entry tolerance 1e-8 A).
No atom permutation, rigid alignment, strain removal or trajectory unwrapping
is performed. Cell rows are lattice vectors. For atom i displacement is
mobile_cart[i] + image_shift[i] @ reference_cell - reference_cart[i].
Fractional source coordinates must be finite with abs<=1e6. Volume>=1e-8 A^3
and perpendicular cell heights>=1e-5 A are required. Exact reciprocal-height
bounds enumerate at most 1e6 total image candidates; exceeding this rejects
the entire call before enumeration. No [-1,1] assumption is made for skew
cells. Images within 1e-8 A of the minimum are treated as tied: the
lexicographically smallest image is returned, with tie_count and unique flag.
A half-cell displacement therefore need not have a unique direction.
Source SHA256 identifies actual input bytes. This geometric primitive does
not infer diffusion, atomic identity correspondence, or a physical pathway.

Returns displacements, site_count, species, cell_angstrom, reference_source_file, mobile_source_file, reference_source_sha256, mobile_source_sha256, tie_tolerance_angstrom, cell_tolerance_angstrom, image_candidate_bound, scope. Scientific units, source identity and failure boundaries are described in the field schema and implementation documentation.

MolecularElectronicDescriptors: Compute selected RDKit electronic features from exactly one SMILES or CSV source. Supply exactly one of smiles or csv_file; CSV requires explicit SMILES columns. Both transports use the same named descriptors and scientific settings. CSV preserves source fields, zero-based row identity, selected names, SHA256 provenance and indexed invalid-cell errors in a new streamed artifact. Repeated exact SMILES are computed once per call. Invalid cells fail by default; invalid_policy=record writes null with an indexed error. Limits:10000 transformed cells,16 columns,25 MiB input,128 MiB output. Inline input rejects columns and nondefault invalid_policy. No imputation, training, response selection or scientific workflow is performed. Default names: MaxEStateIndex, MinAbsEStateIndex, MinEStateIndex, qed, NumValenceElectrons, NumRadicalElectrons, MaxPartialCharge, MinPartialCharge, MaxAbsPartialCharge, MinAbsPartialCharge, MolLogP and MolMR. descriptors may select a unique nonempty subset. One parsed hydrogen-suppressed molecule shares EState extrema, Wildman-Crippen logP/MR and one12-iteration Gasteiger charge assignment; missing parameters and nonfinite values fail. MinAbsPartialCharge follows RDKit's named descriptor: the smaller absolute signed minimum/maximum charge, not the minimum over every atom. QED is a model-defined composite, not measured drug-likeness. These features do not estimate experimental charge, activity or partition measurements.
MolecularElectronicDescriptors(smiles: str | None=None, descriptors: list[str] | None=None, csv_file: str | None=None, columns: list[str] | None=None, invalid_policy: str='error') -> dict

Exactly one input_mode branch: inline preserves the existing complete scientific molecular result; csv applies that same calculation to explicit source columns and returns a new artifact, stable source_row_index, SHA256 provenance, settings and indexed errors. Source columns and order are preserved; CSV feature cells are complete JSON and require explicit decoding/extraction for numeric ML arrays. Inline gasteiger_iterations is12 only for a selected partial-charge feature, otherwise null. operation_counts measures explicit selected-feature kernel calls and excludes QED-internal computation. CSV operation_counts instead records input cells and unique cached molecular transformations.

MolecularFingerprint: Calculate molecular fingerprints from exactly one SMILES or explicit CSV source. Algorithms: morgan, rdkit (path), atom_pair, torsion, maccs, avalon, pharm2d, mhfp, secfp, tautomer_target. options accepts only algorithm-specific keys, rejecting irrelevant settings. Morgan defaults radius2/2048 bits; rdkit defaults 2048 bits/path1-7/2 bits per hash/use_hs true/no density folding. atom_pair defaults un-hashed counts; presence must be explicit. Outputs use full sparse indices/counts or minhash values, never abbreviated NumPy text. No salt/tautomer/stereo normalization is applied; removable H are suppressed. Supply exactly one of smiles or csv_file. CSV requires 1-16 named SMILES columns; source fields, zero-based row identity, SHA256 provenance and full JSON fingerprint cells are preserved in a new streamed artifact. Exact repeated SMILES are computed once per CSV call. invalid_policy=error fails and removes a partial artifact; record writes null and indexed errors for invalid cells. Limits are 10000 transformed cells, 25 MiB input and128 MiB output. Inline mode rejects columns and nondefault invalid_policy. No model training, feature selection, response selection or scientific workflow is run.
MolecularFingerprint(smiles: str | None=None, algorithm: str='morgan', options: dict | None=None, csv_file: str | None=None, columns: list[str] | None=None, invalid_policy: str='error') -> dict
smiles: typing.Optional[str]; algorithm: str; options: typing.Optional[dict]; csv_file: typing.Optional[str]; columns: typing.Optional[list[str]]; invalid_policy: str

Exactly one input_mode branch: inline preserves the existing complete scientific molecular result; csv applies that same calculation to explicit source columns and returns a new artifact, stable source_row_index, SHA256 provenance, settings and indexed errors. Source columns and order are preserved; CSV feature cells are complete JSON and require explicit decoding/extraction for numeric ML arrays. Algorithm-specific settings are required only for that algorithm. Inline payload representation is disjoint: bits/on_bits, sparse_counts/counts or minhash/values. Effective length is backend metadata and can differ from requested bits under explicit RDKit density folding.

NeEMO: Submit or resume public NeEMO structure preparation and optional mutation stability jobs. Top-level status is queued until the structure and every requested mutation job finish, then completed; queued results are pending work, not completed predictions. Only parsed completed mutation tables supply kcal/mol stability changes. When the structure job is queued, local preparation from the first PDB model reports isolated-chain Shrake-Rupley absolute ASA in angstrom^2, distinct from NeEMO relative accessibility percent. No stability change is estimated locally. The same mutation and settings reuse the stored PID.
NeEMO(pdb_id: str, chain: str='', mutation: str='', temperature: float=20.0, ph: float=8.5, wait_seconds: int=150, poll_seconds: int=8)
pdb_id: str; chain: str; mutation: str; temperature: float; ph: float; wait_seconds: int; poll_seconds: int

NeEMO JSON with required top-level status queued/completed, source-traced branch-specific preparation, resumable job identifiers and optional actual mutation results. A queued structure includes local isolated-chain absolute ASA from the first PDB model, not NeEMO relative accessibility. Completed structure preparation may still accompany a queued mutation job; stability_changes remains empty until that requested mutation job finishes and its table parses. No local stability estimate is supplied.

NumericRangeMask: Compute an ordered 0/1 indicator for explicit numeric bounds, retaining every vector/matrix position. Bound inclusivity is declared; no scientific cutoff or significance decision is inferred.
NumericRangeMask(values: list, lower_bound: float | None=None, upper_bound: float | None=None, lower_inclusive: bool=True, upper_inclusive: bool=True) -> dict
values: list; lower_bound: float | None; upper_bound: float | None; lower_inclusive: bool; upper_inclusive: bool

Return an ordered 0/1 indicator for a declared finite numeric range.

Accept a nonempty finite 1D vector or rectangular 2D matrix, with at most
10000 total cells. Boolean/null cells, ragged or higher-dimensional input
are rejected. Bounds are finite numbers or null; null is unbounded, never
a missing-cell replacement. Inclusive flags must be actual booleans.
A reversed range is an error. Equal endpoints with either endpoint open
produce a valid all-zero mask. Two null bounds produce an all-one mask.
Output numeric 0/1 preserves every input position and shape. No rows are
deleted and no values are imputed. It does not infer a scientific cutoff,
establish statistical significance, or correct sampling/measurement bias.

PDBInterfaceContacts: Protein chain contacts in one explicit PDB model; optional buried SASA. Uses standard amino-acid ATOM residues only, selected Biopython alternate locations, and heavy atoms (H/D excluded). No assembly is inferred or downloaded. Coordinates and molecule/chain identity come from caller's file; contacts do not prove a physiological interaction. PairwiseNumericDistances: Compute a complete pairwise distance matrix on unchanged ordered feature rows using one declared metric. Preserve zero-vector and unit policies; perform no alignment, clustering or representative selection.
PairwiseNumericDistances(values: list, other: list | None=None, metric: str='euclidean') -> dict
values: list; other: list | None; metric: str

Compute one explicitly selected pairwise distance,without preprocessing.

Input rows are finite numeric vectors with equal nonzero feature width;
bool/null,ragged/empty vectors rejected. At most10000 total input numeric
cells and10000 output distances. With other=null compare values with itself;
otherwise columns correspond to other rows. Shared feature order/units are
caller responsibilities. No implicit scaling,imputation or row removal.
Euclidean/cityblock distances inherit feature units only when those units
are commensurate. Cosine returns 1-cos(theta), not the angle theta or Euclidean distance;
it need not satisfy the triangle inequality.
any all-zero row makes it undefined and rejects the whole call.
Bray-Curtis requires nonnegative numeric values;zero-vs-positive is1,
two zero rows have undefined denominator and reject the whole call.
Jaccard requires numeric0/1presence indicators;no automatic binarization.
Following SciPy,empty-versus-empty Jaccard dissimilarity is0 explicitly.
Nonfinite computed distances (including numeric overflow) reject the call.
Distances do not establish statistical independence,causality,cluster
validity or suitability of the selected metric for a scientific question.

PeriodicNeighborList:
Return all directed periodic geometric neighbors in a finite radius.

CIF fractional positions are preserved without rational-coordinate snapping.

Args:
    structure_file: Explicitly uploaded ordered crystal file, same public
        allowlist and10MiB source limit as the other crystal primitives.
    cutoff_angstrom: Finite positive Cartesian radius<=10angstrom. Search
        uses pymatgen's periodic neighbor algorithm, including image shifts
        beyond[-1,1] when required by an oblique cell. At most256 source
        sites and10000 returned directed edges; estimated candidate work
        N²*product(2*ceil((cutoff+1e-8)/h_i)+3) must be<=1000000,where h_i
        are perpendicular cell heights. Excess work/edges reject the whole
        call before return; results are never truncated to the edge limit.

Returns:
    dict with neighbors(list of unique edge_id,center_index,neighbor_index,image_shift,
    distance_angstrom,displacement_angstrom),edge_count,source SHA/formula,
    species,cell_angstrom,cutoff_angstrom,boundary_tolerance_angstrom,
    candidate_pair_bound andscope. Cell vectors are rows. Displacement is
    r_neighbor+image_shift@cell-r_center (center to neighbor-image).
    The list is directed: reverse edges are retained,and same-atom nonzero
    images are valid neighbors. Only the exact self pair with zero image
    is removed; coincident distinct sites are not silently discarded.
    Distances<=cutoff+1e-8angstrom are included. No chemical bonding,
    coordination-shell,oxidation-state or nearest-neighbor interpretation.

Raises:
    ValueError: Unsupported type/radius,disorder,too many sites or images,
        near-singular/nonfinite cell,nonfinite or abs>1e6 fractional
        coordinates,numerical failure or>10000 edges.

Returns neighbors, edge_count, source_file, source_sha256, formula, site_count, species, cell_angstrom, cutoff_angstrom, boundary_tolerance_angstrom, candidate_pair_bound, scope. Scientific units, source identity and failure boundaries are described in the field schema and implementation documentation.

PowderDiffractionPattern:
Compute one ideal powder X-ray pattern from an ordered public structure.

CIF fractional positions are preserved without rational-coordinate snapping.

Args:
    structure_file (str): Uploaded ordered structure file (CIF/POSCAR).
    wavelength_angstrom (float): Positive X-ray wavelength in [0.1,5] angstrom.
    two_theta_min_deg (float): Lower two-theta angle in [0,179) degrees.
    two_theta_max_deg (float): Upper two-theta angle above lower and <=179.

Returns:
    dict: Peak records (two_theta_deg, relative_intensity, d_spacing_angstrom,
        and Miller-index families), wavelength/range, source hash/formula and
        pymatgen version. Intensities are normalized to maximum100; a valid
        range with no reflections returns an empty peak list. This ideal
        kinematic calculation omits instrumental broadening and texture.

Returns peaks, peak_count, wavelength_angstrom, two_theta_range_deg, formula, source_file, source_sha256, pymatgen_version, limitations. Scientific units, source identity and failure boundaries are described in the field schema and implementation documentation.

Binary Brier/log-loss and fixed equal-width reliability bins.

Empty bins retain null observed/predicted means. Log loss clips only at1e-15
for numerical evaluation and reports this; no model/calibration is fitted. Returned numeric labels use canonical integer representation. Labels are strings or finite mathematical integers. QueryScientificRecordsFile: Filter, project and stably order a public JSON record file with explicit predicates and a typed string/integer identity field. Preserve source provenance and write complete output plus a bounded preview.
QueryScientificRecordsFile(records_file: str, id_field: str, predicates: list | None=None, fields: list | None=None, order_by: list | None=None, limit: int | None=None, preview_limit: int=20) -> dict
records_file: str; id_field: str; predicates: list | None; fields: list | None; order_by: list | None; limit: int | None; preview_limit: int

Filter,project and order public/file-artifact records without code execution.

records_file is uploaded or an explicit current-task artifact JSON record
list,or an object with data;0..60000 rows,25 MiB maximum. Every record must have
a unique nonempty string id_field. No identifier conversion/deduplication.

predicates is null or up to32 AND-connected objects with field,op,value.
Operators:eq,ne,lt,le,gt,ge,in,not_in,is_null,is_not_null,exists,missing.
eq/ne/in/not_in compare JSON scalar types exactly except numeric1==1.0;
bool is distinct from number. in/not_in value is1..1000 scalars. Other binary
operators take a scalar value;numeric operators require finite numbers.
Unary operators must omit value. Null numeric comparisons return false;
missing predicate fields raise except for explicit exists/missing tests.
Nested field paths,regex,arbitrary expressions and OR are not supported.

fields is null for all fields or up to 256 unique top-level field names;ID
always retained. Every selected requested field must exist;null is retained.
order_by is null or up to 8 objects:{field,direction:'ascending'|'descending',
nulls:'first'|'last'}. Direction defaults ascending,nulls last. Non-null sort
values per key must be one comparable scalar family(number,string,bool).
Missing sort fields and mixed scalar families raise. Ties retain source
order. limit is null or0..60000,applied after filtering and sorting;full
matching count is always returned independently from output count.

Full output records and original non-data metadata are written atomically
under the explicit task-local artifact root,with source/result SHA256 and
exact query parameters. preview_limit0..100 returns complete projected rows
up to20000 characters,without altering artifact selection. Empty results are
valid. No threshold,hypothesis family,background,scientific unit or method
is inferred,and no sampling or missing-value imputation occurs.

SliceNumericArray(values: list, start: int=0, stop: int | None=None, step: int=1) -> dict
values: list; start: int; stop: int | None; step: int

Select existing rows/elements, preserving supplied values and order.

values is a nonempty finite real vector or rectangular matrix, excluding
booleans/strings/null, with outer length and total cells <=10000 and matrix
width <=1000. A matrix must have at least one column. Select only along the
outer axis: start/stop are nonnegative integers <= original outer length,
stop is exclusive (null means length), step is an integer1..10000. Negative
indexing, clipping out-of-bounds indices and reverse order are unsupported.
stop<=start yields a valid empty selection. Explicit output_shape preserves
a matrix's column width even when values is empty. No arithmetic, imputation,
sorting, unit inference, file I/O or code execution occurs.
